problemText: Coal is formed primarily from which organic material that was compressed and heated over millions of years?
choices: Marine organisms such as diatoms and algae deposited on the ocean floor
Ancient swamp vegetation including ferns, mosses, and woody plants buried in waterlogged sediments
Decayed animal carcasses buried in desert sediments under arid conditions
Volcanic mineral deposits mixed with surface plant matter
hints: Think about swampy, oxygen-poor environments that would prevent decomposition.
Peat bogs are an early stage in coal formation.

problemText: A coal-fired power plant receives 500 megajoules (MJ) of chemical energy from burning coal and delivers 175 MJ as electricity to the grid, with the remainder lost as waste heat. Calculate the plant's thermal efficiency as a percentage. Round to the nearest whole number.
hints: Efficiency (%) = (useful energy output / total energy input) × 100.

problemText: Hydraulic fracturing (fracking) is used to extract natural gas from shale formations by injecting high-pressure fluid underground to crack the rock. Which of the following is the most significant environmental concern specifically associated with this practice?
choices: Contamination of groundwater aquifers from fracking fluids and methane migration through cracks in the wellbore casing
Release of nitrogen oxide gases directly from the high-pressure fracturing equipment
Deforestation of large forested areas to clear land for wellhead installation
Increased ocean acidification near offshore fracking operations
hints: Consider what materials are injected underground and what natural gas could escape through.

problemText: A natural gas water heater has an input rating of 40,000 BTU per hour and operates for 3 hours. Given that 1 BTU = 1,055 joules, calculate the total energy input to the water heater in megajoules (MJ). Round to the nearest whole number. (1 MJ = 1,000,000 J)
hints: First find total BTU (rate × time), then convert BTU to joules, then joules to megajoules.
40,000 BTU/hr × 3 hr = 120,000 BTU; multiply by 1,055 J/BTU then divide by 1,000,000.

problemText: Surface (strip) mining removes coal deposits that lie close to the surface by stripping away the overlying rock and soil (overburden). Which of the following environmental consequences is most specifically associated with surface mining rather than underground shaft mining?
choices: Higher rates of methane gas release from decomposing coal seams in sealed mine shafts
Greater risk of underground subsidence causing sudden collapse of mined tunnels
Increased thermal pollution of deep aquifers from heat generated by underground blasting
Severe removal of topsoil and disruption of overlying ecosystems, along with acid mine drainage when pyrite-bearing rocks are exposed to air and water
hints: Surface mining literally removes the land surface — think about what happens to soil, vegetation, and sulfide minerals exposed to oxygen and rainfall.

problemText: Energy Return on Investment (EROI) measures the ratio of usable energy obtained from a source to the energy required to extract and process it. As conventional oil reserves become depleted and producers shift to unconventional sources such as oil sands and deep-sea drilling, what is the most likely consequence for net energy available to society?
choices: Net energy available to society increases, because advanced drilling technologies raise the EROI of all unconventional sources above that of conventional oil
Net energy available remains essentially constant, because total global fossil fuel reserves are effectively unlimited
Net energy available to society decreases, because more energy must be invested per unit of fuel extracted, lowering EROI and leaving less energy for end uses
Net energy available is unaffected by EROI, since EROI is a monetary accounting metric rather than a physical energy measure
hints: EROI of oil sands (~3:1) is much lower than conventional oil (~20:1).
If it costs more energy to get energy, less net energy is available for everything else society does.

problemText: In a nuclear power plant, energy is released from uranium-235 fuel. Which of the following best describes the nuclear fission process that produces this energy?
choices: Two small atomic nuclei are combined under extreme heat and pressure to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy
A heavy uranium nucleus absorbs a neutron and splits into smaller nuclei and free neutrons, releasing a large amount of energy
Uranium fuel rods are burned in the presence of oxygen inside a controlled combustion chamber
Uranium atoms are converted directly into electricity through a photovoltaic reaction in the reactor core
hints: Fission means 'splitting.' The opposite process (fusion) combines nuclei.
Neutron absorption triggers the split.

problemText: Ethanol produced by fermenting corn is classified as a biomass fuel and is blended into gasoline in many countries. Which of the following is considered a meaningful environmental advantage of corn ethanol compared to conventional gasoline?
choices: Corn ethanol has a higher energy density per liter than gasoline, reducing total fuel consumption
Burning corn ethanol produces zero carbon dioxide emissions at the tailpipe
Corn is a renewable feedstock that can be regrown annually, unlike finite petroleum reserves
Corn ethanol production requires no agricultural land and can be synthesized entirely from atmospheric carbon
hints: Think about what 'renewable' means in terms of how quickly the feedstock can be replenished.
Corn does release CO2 when burned — the advantage is about the source, not the combustion.

problemText: Strontium-90, a radioactive isotope released in nuclear accidents, has a half-life of 29 years. A nuclear accident deposits 1 kilogram of strontium-90 onto agricultural land. After 87 years, what fraction of the original strontium-90 remains? Express your answer as a decimal (do not round).
hints: Determine how many half-lives fit into 87 years.
After each half-life, the amount is multiplied by 1/2; apply this repeatedly.

problemText: High-level nuclear waste (HLNW) from spent reactor fuel rods poses an extraordinary long-term storage challenge. Which of the following characteristics of HLNW is the primary reason that permanent geological disposal is so difficult to design and guarantee?
choices: High-level nuclear waste rapidly decays to a completely stable, nonradioactive form within 50 years of removal from the reactor
High-level nuclear waste emits only alpha radiation, which can be shielded by a thin paper layer, making containment straightforward
High-level nuclear waste can be chemically neutralized by mixing it with common industrial alkaline compounds
Many isotopes in high-level nuclear waste have half-lives exceeding 10,000 years, requiring isolation from the biosphere far beyond the lifespan of any human institution or storage material
hints: Compare the time scale required for safe storage to the entire recorded history of human civilization.
Plutonium-239 has a half-life of about 24,100 years.

problemText: Proponents of biomass combustion for electricity generation describe it as 'carbon neutral,' arguing that the CO2 released during combustion is offset by CO2 absorbed while the plant material was growing. Critics argue this claim is misleading. Which statement best explains the most important criticism of the carbon-neutral argument for biomass?
choices: Burning biomass does not actually release carbon dioxide, so the term 'carbon neutral' is technically correct by definition
The carbon released when biomass is burned was never originally sequestered from the atmosphere and originated entirely from volcanic sources

The CO2 released during combustion may not be recaptured on the same time scale as combustion — especially if mature forests are cleared for biomass, since regrowing that carbon sink takes decades to centuries
Biomass combustion produces only methane rather than carbon dioxide, making the standard carbon-neutral accounting framework entirely irrelevant
hints: Consider the time lag between emitting CO2 now and re-sequestering it through regrowth.
What if the biomass source is old-growth forest rather than a fast-growing crop?

problemText: A city is deciding between constructing a new nuclear power plant or a new coal-fired power plant of equal generating capacity. Both would operate for 60 years. Which of the following most accurately compares their overall environmental impact over the full life cycle?
choices: Coal plants have substantially lower greenhouse gas emissions over their lifetime because they do not generate radioactive waste that must be monitored for thousands of years

Nuclear plants produce dramatically less air pollution and far fewer lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions than coal plants, but generate high-level radioactive waste requiring permanent geological isolation
Nuclear plants produce significant routine air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions at levels comparable to coal, but benefit from not generating radioactive waste during normal operation
Both options have essentially identical environmental profiles because both rely on nonrenewable mineral resources and involve large-scale industrial operations
hints: Nuclear plants emit no CO2 during operation; coal plants are among the largest single sources of CO2 and SO2.
The key tradeoff for nuclear is the long-term waste problem, not operational air emissions.

problemText: Photovoltaic (PV) solar panels generate electricity directly from sunlight. Which of the following best describes the physical mechanism by which a PV panel produces an electric current?
choices: Sunlight heats a working fluid inside the panel, which expands and spins a small turbine connected to a generator
Incoming photons excite electrons in a semiconductor material (such as silicon), causing them to flow as a direct electric current
Solar panels absorb and store heat during the day, then release it as electrical energy through a thermoelectric cooling effect at night
Mirrors on the panel surface focus sunlight onto a central boiler, generating steam that drives a generator
hints: PV = photovoltaic: 'photo' means light, 'voltaic' refers to electricity.
Semiconductors have a band structure that allows photon-excited electrons to flow freely.

problemText: Large hydroelectric dams generate substantial renewable electricity, but environmental groups frequently oppose new dam construction on major rivers. Which of the following is the most ecologically significant impact of large hydroelectric dams?
choices: Routine emission of sulfur dioxide gas from water turbine operations, contributing to acid deposition downstream
Release of radioactive isotopes from flooded riverbed sediments into downstream drinking water supplies
Rapid depletion of regional groundwater tables due to seepage from the reservoir into surrounding aquifers
Blockage of fish migration routes (such as salmon spawning runs) and disruption of river sediment transport, altering downstream ecosystems and delta formation
hints: Think about a river as a continuous system — what happens to fish that cannot pass the dam?
Sediment trapped behind a dam cannot reach downstream floodplains and deltas.

problemText: Wind energy has grown rapidly as a share of electricity generation in many countries. Despite this growth, grid operators often identify a significant limitation of wind as a primary power source. What is this primary limitation?
choices: Wind turbines emit large quantities of carbon dioxide and nitrogen oxides during operation, similar in magnitude to natural gas plants
Wind turbines cannot be scaled up sufficiently to power large metropolitan areas under any circumstances
Wind is intermittent — its availability is determined by weather patterns and does not reliably coincide with periods of peak electricity demand
Wind turbines require nuclear-grade titanium alloys that make large-scale deployment prohibitively expensive compared to fossil fuels
hints: Consider what happens on a calm, hot summer day when air conditioning demand is highest.
Energy storage and grid management become critical when supply does not match demand timing.

problemText: Geothermal energy taps heat from Earth's interior to generate electricity and provide direct heating. Despite being a reliable, low-emissions energy source, large-scale geothermal development remains geographically limited. Which of the following best explains this geographic restriction?
choices: Geothermal energy requires large ocean surface areas for heat exchange and is therefore unavailable in landlocked regions
Geothermal energy is most accessible where tectonic activity, volcanic hotspots, or plate boundaries bring sufficient heat close enough to the surface for practical extraction
Geothermal plants require enormous flat land areas to install the necessary heat-exchange field arrays, limiting them to wide plains
Geothermal energy depends on permafrost reservoirs and is limited to arctic and subarctic regions where ground temperatures are coldest
hints: Where are the most active geothermal regions in the world? Think Iceland, New Zealand, The Geysers in California.
Earth's average geothermal gradient is too low for most locations — special geology is required.

problemText: A coastal city is evaluating three renewable electricity options: offshore wind, tidal energy, and solar photovoltaic. An energy planner notes that grid reliability is a top priority. Which of the following statements most accurately identifies a key advantage of tidal energy relative to the other two options in terms of grid planning?
choices: Tidal energy generation is highly predictable months or years in advance, because tidal cycles are governed by the gravitational positions of the Moon and Sun — giving it a firm-capacity advantage over both wind and solar
Solar PV is the only option with zero land-use requirements regardless of installation type, making it environmentally superior to wind and tidal in every coastal application
Offshore wind consistently generates more total annual energy than tidal or solar in every coastal geographic location worldwide
All three options emit equivalent quantities of greenhouse gases during operation, so the grid-reliability choice is purely an aesthetic and political decision
hints: Astronomers can predict tides years ahead. Can you say the same for wind or cloud cover?
Firm capacity — energy that is reliably available when needed — is especially valuable to grid operators.

problemText: A proposal is made to build a large concentrated solar power (CSP) plant in a Mojave Desert region to replace a coal-fired plant of equal generating capacity. The CSP facility would occupy 50 km² and use wet cooling (water-cooled condensers). An environmental review is required. Which of the following represents the most analytically complete assessment of the proposal's environmental trade-offs?
choices: The proposal is unambiguously beneficial because CSP produces no greenhouse gases during operation, making all concerns about land use, water consumption, and local ecology secondary and negligible
The proposal should be rejected outright because any industrial land use in a desert environment is ecologically unacceptable, regardless of the climate benefits

The net environmental benefit depends on a full accounting that weighs substantial reductions in greenhouse gas and criteria air pollutant emissions against habitat disruption for desert species, significant water consumption for steam cooling in an arid region, and potential effects on local surface albedo and microclimate
Since deserts support no significant biodiversity or ecosystem services, the only relevant criterion is the levelized cost of electricity compared to the coal plant
hints: Mojave Desert is home to the threatened desert tortoise and many endemic species — 'empty' does not mean 'ecologically valueless.'
CSP wet-cooling can consume millions of gallons of water per year in a region with extreme water scarcity.

problemText: The United States Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards are a federal policy tool aimed at reducing transportation energy consumption. How do CAFE standards achieve this goal?
choices: They set a federal minimum price per gallon of gasoline to discourage excessive driving
They require automobile manufacturers to meet specified average fuel efficiency targets (in miles per gallon) across the entire fleet of vehicles they sell each model year
They mandate that all newly manufactured passenger vehicles must be powered exclusively by electricity or hydrogen by a set deadline
They require vehicle owners to purchase annual fuel-efficiency compliance certificates proportional to their annual mileage
hints: CAFE = Corporate Average Fuel Economy — the 'average' is across all vehicle models a manufacturer sells.
It regulates the producers (automakers), not the buyers or fuel prices directly.

problemText: Cogeneration (also called combined heat and power, or CHP) systems can achieve overall efficiencies of 70–90%, far higher than a conventional power plant's typical 33–40% efficiency. What is the fundamental reason cogeneration achieves such dramatically higher overall efficiency?
choices: Cogeneration systems capture and productively use the waste heat that a conventional power plant would simply reject into a river, lake, or cooling tower
Cogeneration units use high-grade nuclear fuel with a greater energy content per kilogram than the coal or natural gas used by conventional plants
Cogeneration equipment burns fuel at significantly lower combustion temperatures, which reduces thermodynamic losses from the Rankine cycle
Cogeneration plants bypass the steam turbine entirely, eliminating all mechanical friction losses associated with rotating machinery
hints: A conventional power plant discards roughly 60% of its fuel energy as waste heat. What if that heat had a use?
Industrial facilities, hospitals, and district heating networks are common cogeneration customers.

problemText: A homeowner replaces a 60-watt incandescent bulb with a 9-watt LED bulb that produces equivalent light output. Beyond the direct reduction in the homeowner's electricity bill, which of the following describes an important broader environmental benefit of widespread LED adoption?
choices: LED bulbs release oxygen as a chemical byproduct of their semiconductor operation, measurably improving indoor air quality
LED bulbs emit a narrow band of ultraviolet radiation that catalytically breaks down indoor volatile organic compound (VOC) pollutants on wall surfaces
Because LEDs draw far less power from the grid, power plants burn less fossil fuel to meet demand, reducing emissions of carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide, and nitrogen oxides
LED bulbs generate their own supplementary electricity through embedded micro-photovoltaic cells, reducing demand on transmission lines
hints: Trace the energy savings upstream from the socket back to the power plant.
Less grid demand directly translates to less fuel burned at generating stations.

problemText: A homeowner replaces a 60-watt incandescent bulb with a 9-watt LED bulb of equivalent brightness. The bulb is used 4 hours per day for 365 days per year. Electricity costs 0.12 dollars per kWh. Calculate the homeowner's annual electricity cost savings in dollars. Round to the nearest cent.
hints: Power saved = 60 W − 9 W = 51 W. Convert to kW (divide by 1,000), then multiply by hours of use per year to get kWh saved.
Annual hours = 4 h/day × 365 days = 1,460 h; cost saved = kWh saved × 0.12 dollars/kWh.

problemText: An architect designing a new home in a temperate Northern Hemisphere climate wants to minimize heating energy costs through passive solar design, without adding any active mechanical systems. Which combination of design features is most characteristic of a well-executed passive solar building?
choices: Installing a large array of photovoltaic panels on the roof to generate electricity for electric resistance baseboard heaters throughout the home

Orienting large, high-quality windows on the south-facing wall to capture low winter sun, combined with high-thermal-mass materials (such as concrete or tile floors) that absorb daytime heat and release it gradually at night
Painting the entire exterior of the building bright white to reflect all incoming solar radiation and prevent any solar heat gain in all seasons
Installing small wind turbines on the roofline to power electric radiators positioned in each room of the building
hints: 'Passive' means no mechanical systems — the design itself does the work.
Thermal mass stores heat; south-facing windows in the Northern Hemisphere receive the most winter sun.

problemText: A municipal energy planner is comparing two strategies to reduce natural gas use in city-owned buildings: Strategy 1 — retrofit all municipal buildings with high-efficiency insulation and HVAC systems (demand-side management); Strategy 2 — build a cogeneration plant to supply both heat and electricity simultaneously to municipal buildings. Which of the following most accurately captures the key trade-offs between these two strategies?
choices: Strategy 1 is always the superior choice because reducing demand at the point of use is inherently more effective than any supply-side improvement, regardless of the specific efficiency characteristics involved
Strategy 2 is always the superior choice because cogeneration plants carry higher efficiency ratings in engineering specifications than any achievable insulation improvement

Strategy 1 reduces total energy consumption at the point of use, lowering both fuel input and associated emissions; Strategy 2 extracts more useful output from the fuel that is burned — both can meaningfully reduce net gas consumption, but they differ in upfront capital cost, ongoing maintenance, and the scale at which savings are realized
Neither strategy reduces greenhouse gas emissions because both approaches still rely on burning natural gas in the same city infrastructure, with no net change in total combustion
hints: These strategies attack waste at different points in the energy chain — one reduces demand, the other improves supply efficiency.
Consider that both can reduce total gas consumption but through fundamentally different mechanisms with different cost structures.
